key_insight: WOVEN shows that many multimodal LLM failures stem from a shared weakness in visual transition reasoning, and that this skill can be trained as a reusable foundation across tasks.
engineering_relevance: For model builders, WOVEN provides a practical data-and-training recipe to improve spatial, embodied, physical, and temporal understanding with better transfer than task-specific fine-tuning.
method: Built WOVEN as a benchmark and training source with 36,076 realistic rollout examples.
Structured supervision by scene, action, and reasoning type across 20 scene types, 5 action types, and 8 reasoning types.
Evaluated 38 frontier MLLMs, then trained models at multiple scales to test transfer and derive a training recipe.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that even top models lag far behind humans, while WOVEN-trained subsets of about 2,000 items each improved 22 of 26 external benchmarks and could replace 30–50% of task-specific data.
watch_item: The gains depend on carefully choosing supervision by reasoning operation and on large visual state changes, so naive dataset mixing may not reproduce the same transfer.
paper_title: WOVEN: Weaving Visual World Modeling into Multimodal LLMs
